questions.q: Why is storing a large training dataset directly in a git repository unworkable?
options: Git cannot store binary files at all
Git keeps every historical version of every tracked file forever, so cloning the repo means downloading every past version, not just the current one
Git repositories have a hard 1GB size limit enforced by the git protocol itself
Git only supports text files, never datasets
questions.explain: Git's full-history model is fine for megabytes of code but unworkable for gigabytes of data, since every version ever committed stays in the repo's history and gets downloaded on clone.

questions.q: How does DVC keep a git repo small while still versioning large datasets?
options: It compresses the dataset and stores the compressed version directly in git
It tracks a lightweight pointer file (a content hash and metadata) in git, while the actual data lives in a separate remote like S3
It deletes old dataset versions automatically after each commit
It stores the dataset as a git submodule inside the same repository
questions.explain: DVC commits a small .dvc pointer file to git containing a content hash, while the real data is pushed to and pulled from a separate remote storage location, keeping the git repo itself small.

questions.q: What does 'content-addressed storage' mean in the context of DVC or git?
options: Data is identified by its filename and folder path
Data is identified by a hash of its actual content, so identical content always produces the same hash regardless of filename
Data is identified by the date and time it was uploaded
Data is identified by the IP address of the machine that uploaded it
questions.explain: Content-addressed storage hashes the actual bytes of the data, making 'is this the same dataset version' a precise, checkable question rather than relying on filenames, sizes, or modification dates, which can be misleading.

questions.q: What happens when you run `git checkout <old-commit>` followed by `dvc pull` in a DVC-tracked repo?
options: Nothing changes, since DVC does not interact with git history
The old commit's matching .dvc pointer is checked out, and dvc pull fetches the exact data version that pointer refers to
It deletes the current dataset version permanently
It always re-downloads the entire dataset history, not just one version
questions.explain: Because the .dvc pointer file is versioned in git like any other file, checking out an old commit also checks out the matching pointer, and dvc pull then fetches exactly the data version that pointer refers to.

questions.q: What does logging a DVC data hash alongside a git commit hash in an experiment-tracking run accomplish?
options: It makes the training run execute faster
It completes the provenance picture: code (commit hash), configuration (resolved config snapshot), and data (DVC hash) all become recoverable for that run
It replaces the need to log the git commit hash at all
It is only useful for debugging GPU memory issues
questions.explain: Combined with the commit-hash logging from Lesson 16 and Hydra's resolved config snapshot from Lesson 12, logging the data version closes the remaining gap in answering 'what exactly produced this number' -- without relying on a manual note.
